summary: Siyong Liang (1904–1954) was a scholar in history and archaeology. He studied at Tsinghua University and at Harvard University around 1924 to 1930.

Smita Halder is a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. Supervised by Susmita Basu Majumdar for doctoral studies, she is attested in 2026 as a Research Scholar / Fellow at The Asiatic Society.

So Takahashi is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who earned an M.A. from the University of Tokyo. Takahashi was an associate professor (attested 1977–1978) and later a professor (attested 1991) at Meijo University.

Sodo Mori (b. 1934), a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar, studied at Komazawa and Tokyo universities under Kogen Mizuno, Hajime Nakamura, and G. P. Malalasekera. Mori held posts at Josai, Kelaniya, and Aichi Gakuin University (1991–2003).
Sodo Yokoyama (1907–1980) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Antai-ji from 1949 to 1957 under Kodo Sawaki, as well as under Eko Hashimoto.
Soen Nakagawa (1907–1984) worked in Buddhist studies. Nakagawa studied at First Higher School, Japan, the University of Tokyo (~1927–1930), and under traditional teacher Gempo Yamamoto (~1931–1961).

Sogen Omori (1904–1994) worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Nihon University and under Seisetsu Seki, Bokuo Seki, and Jirōkichi Yamada, serving as professor (1970) and president (1978–1982) at Hanazono University.

Sogyal Rinpoche (1947–2019) was a Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology figure. He studied at the University of Delhi, Cambridge, and under Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, among others, founding Rigpa in 1975.

Soiku Shigematsu (b. 1943) studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, University of Tokyo, and Kyoto University. He taught English literature at Shizuoka University (1975–2001) and was a professor at Kansai Medical University (2001–2006).
Sojo Hirano (1930–2011) was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as an assistant professor at Hanazono University (attested 1974) and as shike at Zuigan-ji (attested 1992–1996).

Sokatsu Shaku (1870–1954) was a Buddhist studies master who studied under Kosen Imakita (1889) and Soyen Shaku (1893–1898). He founded Tokyo Ryōbōkai in 1901, Ryobokai Dojo of North America in 1906, and Ningen Zen Kyōdan.

Sokei-an Shigetsu Sasaki (1882–1945) was a Buddhist studies master. He studied at Tokyo Fine Arts School and California School of Design, and under Sokatsu Shaku and Soyen Shaku, later founding the First Zen Institute of America in 1930.

Sokichi Tsuda (1873–1961) was a scholar in history, philosophy, and sinology who studied at Tōkyō Senmon Gakkō. He held posts at the SMR Research Department (~1908–1919), University of Tokyo (~1920–1923), and Waseda University (~1918–1940).

Soko Morinaga (1925–1995) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyama High School, Daitoku-ji, and under Sesso Oda and Zuigan Goto. Morinaga served as head of Hanazono University (1986–1994) and chief priest at Daishuin (~1963–1995).

Sokuo Eto (1888–1958) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa, Kyoto, and Tokyo universities. He served as president of Komazawa Junior College (~1950–1953) and became a professor at Komazawa University in 1953.

Solomon George FitzHerbert is a Tibetology scholar who earned a doctorate at the University of Oxford. He has served as a departmental lecturer at Oxford and as a researcher at the National Centre for Scientific Research (attested 2019).
Soma Thera (1898–1960) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at St. Benedict's College, Colombo, and under Jetavana Sayadaw in 1936. He was a member of the Servants of the Buddha (~1926–1936).

Somadeva Vasudeva is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned a PhD at Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. Vasudeva held posts at the French Institute of Pondicherry, Kyoto University (professor, 2011), and Columbia University as assistant professor.

Somboon Watana works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, completing a PhD at Panjab University (1999) under Rekha Jhanji and Dharmanand Sharma. Watana is an assistant professor at Mahidol University (attested 2026).

Somchai Kusalacitto works in Buddhist studies and philosophy, holding a Ph.D. from the University of Madras. Kusalacitto served as dean and deputy rector for foreign affairs at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2003).
